card.summary: A single‑storey, 4‑room colonial bungalow with white shingle siding, hardwood floors, and period‑appropriate detailing.
card.description: The Desoto‑inspired colonial bungalow stands proudly on a 792 cm by 1417 cm lot, its single‑storey silhouette capped by a modest 250 cm roofline. White shingle siding wraps the rectangular envelope, echoing the tidy, early‑20th‑century aesthetic while the asphalt‑shingled roof adds a subtle texture. Four well‑proportioned rooms—two bedrooms, a living area, and a kitchen with a dedicated breakfast nook—share a single, well‑ventilated bathroom, all arranged to minimize circulation and maximize daylight. Interior walls of 10 cm wood studs support drywall finished in crisp white paint, creating a bright canvas for furnishings. Six sliding aluminum‑frame windows punctuate the façade, each opening to invite breezes into the living and kitchen spaces. Solid‑wood entry and back doors swing on sturdy hinges, while the hardwood oak flooring runs continuously beneath the kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanity, and living‑room area, lending warmth and durability. The roof’s gentle pitch is supported by evenly spaced rafters and finished with a second layer of asphalt shingles, protecting the home from the elements. Modern conveniences—electrical wiring, PVC plumbing, and concealed HVAC ductwork—are discreetly integrated, preserving the historic character while delivering contemporary comfort.
plan: Measure the lot boundaries, confirm the 792 cm by 1417 cm footprint, and stake out the foundation lines.
Draft a full‑scale set of construction drawings, including floor plan, elevations, and roof framing, then obtain the required permits.
Excavate the site, pour a reinforced concrete slab foundation, and install perimeter drainage.
Erect wood stud walls, apply plywood sheathing, and cover the exterior with white shingle siding and asphalt roof shingles.
Install interior partitions, drywall, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems, then finish with hardwood flooring and paint.
Fit all doors, windows, fixtures, and cabinetry, perform a final inspection, and hand over the completed bungalow.

The wall colour is not given; a classic white finish is assumed to complement the shingle exterior.
A porch is not mentioned in the source plan, so the house is designed without a front porch.
Standard modern building codes are assumed for ceiling height (250 cm) and structural spacing.
questions: Do you require any specific interior finishes (e.g., tile versus carpet) beyond the hardwood flooring mentioned?

Is there a preferred orientation for the windows to optimize solar gain or views?

card.description: The Crib Bungalow presents a tidy colonial silhouette with a crisp white shingle envelope that reads gracefully from the street. Measuring 792 cm wide by 1417 cm deep, the single‑storey volume rises 300 cm to a modest roofline capped in matching asphalt shingles. Inside, a compact layout of four rooms—two bedrooms, a living area, and a kitchen—optimises circulation for a modern household. The front entry is framed by a solid wood door on a hinge, while sliding glass windows admit daylight to the living space and bedrooms. A built‑in kitchen cabinet wall runs along the east side, and a dedicated utility corner houses a metal‑cased washing machine ready for daily laundry. White‑washed interior walls, vinyl flooring, and simple crown mouldings give the home a clean, timeless feel. The modest roof pitch, modest eaves, and balanced proportions echo the 1920s pattern‑book bungalow while providing all contemporary comforts. Every component—from the concrete slab foundation to the final ceiling light—fits within the envelope, ensuring a coherent, buildable design.
plan: Measure the lot and stake out a 792 cm by 1417 cm rectangle for the foundation.
Draft a full set of construction drawings in 2‑D and 3‑D, including floor plan, elevations, and sections.
Excavate, pour a 15 cm thick concrete slab foundation, and allow it to cure.
Erect wood stud walls to a height of 250 cm, sheathe with OSB, and apply shingle siding.
Install roof trusses, decking, and shingle roofing, then fit windows, doors, and interior finishes.
Connect all mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services, place the washing machine, and perform a final inspection.
assumptions: The exterior wall colour is assumed to be white, a common finish for colonial bungalows of the 1920s.
Standard ceiling height of 250 cm plus roof structure yields a total building height of 300 cm.
A vinyl floor finish is chosen for durability and ease of installation in a modest residence.
No garage is provided, matching the original Desoto pattern‑book plan which omitted a carport.
questions: Should the front entry include a porch or stoop, or remain a simple step onto the slab?
Do you prefer a single‑pane or double‑pane glazing for the sliding windows?
Is a dedicated laundry room required, or is the washing machine acceptable in a shared utility corner?
